newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX expiring May crude lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX expiring May crude lower on profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX crude futures turned lower at the open Tuesday as profit-taking on the expiring May futures contract erased earlier gains, traders said.
The May contract was down 11 cents at $20.27 a barrel at 1016 EDT, having been up as high as $20.55 a barrel. June crude was up a cent at $20.08.
"There was profit-taking right at the open and now we'll wait and see if there is more short-covering at $20.25," said Nauman Barakat, an oil trader at Prudential Securities.
"We're going to see a lot of volatility in that (May/June) spread today," he added.
May gasoline was off 1.00 cent at 61.80 cents a gallon while May heating oil was off 0.73 cent at 54.75 cents a gallon after crude sharpened its losses to down 61 cents.
"I would have thought that some of the news items would have kept us higher, but crude got wacked at the open, and we are following it down," said a New York gasoline trader.

Dealers said much of crude's weakness was liquidation of length in the May/June spread which had accumulated on expectations that the backwardation would continue to steepen on expiry. May/June had moved from contango April 14 to a 31 cent backwardation on Monday.
Contango means the nearer contract is cheaper than the later one and backwardation means the nearer contract is more expensive.
By 1056 EDT the spread had fallen to steady, leading dealers to call into question whether the bullish footing oil prices managed to gain over the past week will persist.

"Much of the move has been propped up by short covering in May ahead of the expiration today. It's going to be hard to see whether this can last, although some of the strength did spill into the back months," said a New York crude dealer.
May crude's losses accelerated on technical selling after breaking support at around $19.80, the spot month's simple 20-day moving average, dealers said.
Bearish sentiment also stemmed from expectations that there would be crude stock build in this evening's weekly oil inventory report by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
"Another build in crude stocks can not be a good sign," said a trader, noting this would be the seventh consecutive weekly build in crude stocks.
